source_text: Εἰ δέ τις ἑτέρῳ ἐπιβουλεύει, λέληθεν αὑτὸν ὡς ἑαυτῷ πρώτῳ καὶ μόνῳ ἔνεδρον ἐργάζεται. Ὁ δὲ καθαιρῶν ἄλλου ἀσφάλειαν, περιπεσεῖται ὄφεως δήγματι. Ἀλλὰ μὴ [ἴσ. μὴν] ὁ λίθους ἐξαιρούμενος, ὑποίσει πόνον οὐ μικρόν· ἀλλὰ καὶ σχίζων ξύλα, ἐν αὐτῷ τῷ οἰκείῳ ὅπλῳ τὸν κίνδυνον οἴσει. Ἐὰν δὲ συμβῇ τοῦ στελεοῦ τὸν πέλεκυν ἐκπηδῆσαι, θορυβηθήσεται ὁ ταῦτα ἐργαζόμενος, οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῷ συγκομίζων, καὶ ἐπαύξων αὐτὸς τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἄδικον καὶ ὠκύμορον δύναμιν. Ὄφεως δὲ δῆγμα λαθραῖον· οὐδὲν παραμυθήσονται οἱ ἐπᾴδοντες· μάταιοι γάρ εἰσιν. Ἀλλ᾽ ὁ μὲν ἀγαθὸς ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὰ ἐργάζεται αὑτῷ τε καὶ τοῖς πλησίον· ὁ δὲ ἄφρων εἰς ὄλεθρον ἐμπεσεῖται διὰ τῆς αὐτοῦ φλυαρίας. Καὶ ἄπαξ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα, ἄρχεται ἀφρόνως, καὶ παύεται ταχέως, διὰ παντὸς ἐνδεικνύμενος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ ἄνοιαν.
thought_title: Treachery rebounds and foolish talk destroys
orientation: Solomon continues his teaching on the self-destructive nature of treachery and the ruinous character of idle talk, contrasting the good man's beneficial works with the fool's path to destruction.
pass_a_gloss: But if anyone plots against another, he has escaped notice of himself as for himself first and only he works a snare. But the one pulling down another's safety will fall by a serpent's bite. But let not [or: surely not] the one removing stones be weary with toil not small; but also splitting wood, in his own very tool he will bear the danger. But if it happens that the axe flies off from the handle, the one working these things will be troubled, not bringing it together for good, and he himself increasing his own unjust and swift-fated power. A serpent's bite is hidden; nothing will comfort those chanting over it; for they are empty. But the good man works good things for himself and for those nearby; but the fool will fall into destruction through his own idle talk. And once he opens his mouth, he begins foolishly, and he ceases quickly, through it all showing his own folly.

lemmas.gloss: has escaped notice, is hidden from
will be weary, will toil hard

choices.english: he has escaped notice of himself
choices.why: Reflects the reflexive irony: the plotter is hidden from his own awareness while thinking he hides from others; literal sense of λανθάνω + reflexive pronoun.
ἐργάζομαι with object = to work, fashion, prepare; the snare is the product of his plotting, not merely a metaphor.
Genitive of agent/source after περιπεσεῖται; matches Ecclesiastes 10:8-9 LXX imagery of quarrying stones and splitting wood bringing danger.

choices.english: let not [or: surely not] the one removing stones
choices.why: Bracketed variants in source; μὴ gives prohibition, μὴν gives strong affirmation; both possible in transmitted text.
ἐπαείδω = to sing over, chant incantations; context of serpent bite suggests magical/therapeutic chanting, not general 'consolers'.
ὠκύμορος = swift of fate, quickly doomed; describes the fool's power as self-destructively brief, not merely 'hasty'.
Glossary-locked term; denotes empty, wandering speech that brings no benefit, distinct from mere 'foolishness'.

bible_refs.note: He who digs a pit falls into it; he who breaks a hedge, a serpent bites him; he who quarries stones is hurt by them; he who splits wood is endangered by it; if the iron is blunt, he sharpens it; a serpent bites when uncharmed.
The words of a wise man's mouth win favor; the lips of a fool consume him; the beginning of his mouth is folly, the end of his talk is wicked madness; a fool multiplies words.

pass_b_english: If someone plots against another, it escapes his notice that he is setting a snare for himself first and alone. The one who pulls down another's safety will fall foul of a serpent's bite. Moreover, the one who quarries stones will endure no small toil; and even the one splitting wood will carry the danger in his own tool. If the ax head should fly off the handle, the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, since he gathers for no good purpose and only enlarges his own unjust and short-lived power. A serpent's bite is hidden; those chanting over it will comfort no one, for they are empty. But the good person works good for himself and for his neighbors, while the fool will fall into ruin through his own idle talk. And once he has opened his mouth, he begins foolishly and stops quickly, showing his folly all the way through.
notes: Source text bracket [ἴσ. μὴν] indicates textual uncertainty between μὴ (prohibitive) and μὴν (strong affirmative particle); both readings affect sense but not overall argument.
Verb ὑποίσει (future of ὑπορέω) rare; sense 'will be weary with toil' from context of labor.
Compound ὠκύμορον hapax in this work; formed from ὠκύς + μόρος.

problems.quote: Let not the one removing stones toil hard at no small labor;
problems.source_quote: Ἀλλὰ μὴ [ἴσ. μὴν] ὁ λίθους ἐξαιρούμενος, ὑποίσει πόνον οὐ μικρόν
problems.why: The source is a future statement (ἀλλὰ μήν, 'moreover'), not a prohibition. The English turns it into a command and garbles the sense.
problems.fix: Moreover, the one who quarries stones will endure no small toil;

problems.why: συγκομίζων means gathering or amassing, and οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῷ means 'to no good end'. 'Recovering it' invents an object (the ax head) that the source lacks.
problems.fix: gathering his gains to no good end, and he himself increases his own unjust and short-lived power.

problems.quote: will fall into it by a serpent's bite
problems.why: The dative is what he falls foul of—a serpent's bite—not an unstated 'it' or the means.
problems.fix: will fall foul of a serpent's bite.
problems.ruling: περιπεσεῖται ὄφεως δήγματι means 'will fall into a serpent's bite'. The added 'it' and the instrumental 'by' make the bite the means, which misleads.

edits.old: Let not the one removing stones toil hard at no small labor; and even the one splitting wood will carry the danger in his own tool.
edits.new: Moreover, the one who quarries stones will endure no small toil; and even the one splitting wood will carry the danger in his own tool.

edits.old: If the ax head should fly off the handle, the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, not recovering it for good, and he increases his own unjust and swift-fated power.
edits.new: If the ax head should fly off the handle, the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, gathering his gains to no good end, and he himself increases his own unjust and short-lived power.

edits.old: The one who pulls down another's safety will fall into it by a serpent's bite.
edits.new: The one who pulls down another's safety will fall foul of a serpent's bite.

fixed: Changed 'Let not the one removing stones toil hard at no small labor' to 'Moreover, the one who quarries stones will endure no small toil' because the source 'Ἀλλὰ μὴ [ἴσ. μὴν] ὁ λίθους ἐξαιρούμενος, ὑποίσει πόνον οὐ μικρόν' is a future indicative statement ('moreover'), not a prohibition.

Changed 'not recovering it for good' to 'gathering his gains to no good end' because the source 'οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῷ συγκομίζων' means 'gathering/amassing to no good end' with no object 'it' referring to the ax head.

Changed 'will fall into it by a serpent's bite' to 'will fall foul of a serpent's bite' because the source 'περιπεσεῖται ὄφεως δήγματι' uses the dative to indicate what he falls foul of, not an unstated 'it' or the means.

problems.quote: he has escaped notice of himself, for he works a snare for himself first and alone
problems.source_quote: λέληθεν αὑτὸν ὡς ἑαυτῷ πρώτῳ καὶ μόνῳ ἔνεδρον ἐργάζεται
problems.why: λέληθεν αὑτόν means the plot escapes his notice; ὡς gives that unnoticed fact, not a cause.
problems.fix: it escapes him that he is setting a snare for himself first and alone.
problems.ruling: λέληθεν αὑτὸν ὡς … ἐργάζεται means 'he does not realize that he works a snare for himself'. English 'for' makes it causal, and 'escaped notice of himself' is garbled.

edits.old: If someone plots against another, he has escaped notice of himself, for he works a snare for himself first and alone.
edits.new: If someone plots against another, it escapes his notice that he is setting a snare for himself first and alone.

edits.old: the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, gathering his gains to no good end, and he himself increases his own unjust and short-lived power.
edits.new: the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, not bringing it to a good end, and he himself increases his own unjust and short-lived power.

edits.old: those chanting over it will comfort nothing, for they are empty.
edits.new: those chanting over it will comfort no one, for they are empty.

fixed: Changed 'he has escaped notice of himself, for he works a snare' to 'it escapes his notice that he is setting a snare' to reflect λέληθεν αὑτὸν ὡς...ἐργάζεται (the fact escapes him, not a causal 'for').
Changed 'gathering his gains to no good end' to 'not bringing it to a good end' to match οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῷ συγκομίζων (participle, not purpose clause about gains).
Changed 'comfort nothing' to 'comfort no one' because παραμυθήσονται takes personal objects; 'nothing' misstates the verb's valence.

problems.quote: not bringing it to a good end
problems.why: συγκομίζων means gathering or amassing (goods, gain), not bringing a task to an end. The sense is that he amasses for no good purpose.
problems.fix: the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, since he gathers for no good purpose and only enlarges his own unjust and short-lived power.
problems.ruling: συγκομίζων means gathering or amassing; οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῷ is “not for good,” not finishing the work badly.

edits.old: If the ax head should fly off the handle, the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, not bringing it to a good end, and he himself increases his own unjust and short-lived power.
edits.new: If the ax head should fly off the handle, the one doing this work will be thrown into confusion, since he gathers for no good purpose and only enlarges his own unjust and short-lived power.

fixed: Fixed 'not bringing it to a good end' to 'since he gathers for no good purpose' to match συγκομίζων (gathering/amassing) and οὐκ ἐπ᾽ ἀγαθῷ (for no good purpose).
